newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Japan's Hashimoto leaves Indonesia for Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Hashimoto leaves Indonesia for Vietnam.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto left Indonesia for Vietnam on Saturday on the fourth leg of a five-nation tour to consolidate Tokyo's relations with Southeast Asia.

Hashimoto pledged continued support for Indonesia's economic development during his three-day stay in Jakarta, but Japanese officials said a key element of his trip was to boost ties with the members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
The Japanese leader -- who marked his first anniversary in office on Saturday -- is expected to give a key policy address in Singapore on Tuesday.

Japanese sources said Tokyo wanted to move beyond mainly economic ties with ASEAN members as the seven-nation grouping, which marks its 30th anniversary this year, becomes more cohesive and a growing political and economic force in the world.
An expanding ASEAN "provides the core for dramatic regional cooperation", Hashimoto said at a formal dinner hosted by Indonesian President Suharto on Thursday.

Japanese sources said Hashimoto also enunciated two pillars of Japan's foreign policy in talks with Suharto: a continued U.S. military presence to provide stability in the Asia-Pacific region, and active engagement with China to ensure its position in the world and prevent its isolation.
Hashimoto is visiting Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam and Singapore -- all ASEAN states -- on his current tour. He visited the other two ASEAN members, Thailand and the Philippines, last year.

ASEAN leaders agreed at an informal summit in Jakarta on November 30 that Laos, Cambodia and Burma would be admitted to the group, bringing all Southeast Asian nations into the ASEAN fold. This is expected to happen this year but no date was set.
Indonesia's Suharto, the region's elder statesman and a founding father of ASEAN, is due to visit Laos, Cambodia and Burma next month, official sources said on Saturday.

The latest leg of Hashimoto's trip began after Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's government renewed talks late on Friday with Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. The talks aim to negotiate a peaceful solution to the 24-day-old crisis.
